svg.text: Every indexing, scoring and graph algorithm that ships -- where it runs, what it computes, and which are on by default.
3.0.0-alpha.10 + unreleased, index fux.index.v7, analyzer v3, runtime fux.runtime.v9.

ingest and query share one module

PII: pii.toml rules in file order,
256 shards, shard = blake2b(id, 1 byte). One canonical JSONL line per document: sorted keys, no floats, no nulls, NFC. Postings: term hash -> per-field tf
vector, trailing zeros omitted. Record keys: id src loc sha ver mode title phrases terms flen abbr edges archived superseded mtime. The shard header pins
analyzer v3 and the identifier-rules digest. Content is never committed (L3); a use record is never committed (L9).
A committed per-document byte is a function of that document alone. Everything corpus-wide -- df, n, avg_wlen, the anchor fold, the abbr table, communities -- is a read-time fold.
2 - DERIVED PLANE: .fux/runtime/, GITIGNORED, REBUILT FROM THE SHARDS ALONE BY fux build
per-field max tf (mx) and min flen (mnw),
UNWEIGHTED, weighted at query time: an
exact block ceiling, read without the block.

3 - fux ask: THE QUERY PIPELINE, TOP TO BOTTOM
Same analyzer v3 + identifier families -> the REQUIRED hashes, order kept (rank() sums in it). Two expansion layers stack extra hashes at a lower weight,
never new requirements: --expand (agent-written, x 0.2) and corpus-mined Long Form (ABBR) pairs (x 0.5, ON -- W-168 step 4). A doc matching only added words is dropped.
② candidates -- the scan (reference, the DEFAULT)
B2 byte prefilter: each shard line is read as raw bytes and
json.loads'd only if a query hash appears as a substring.
df, n and avg_wlen fall out of the SAME pass -- never stored.
Anchor fold: at/al read off every line; a doc reachable only by
a linker's words is fetched from its one shard (shard_for).
Answers a fresh clone. When the two disagree, this one is right by definition.
② candidates -- the accelerator (--fast, fresh build only)
Terms opened rarest-first. After each term the k-th score θ is
exact. If Σ (deferred terms' block ceilings x Weighting.maximum)
cannot reach θ, every unopened block is skipped -- block-max
pruning. Rounding-aware: skip only if round(bound, 9) < round(θ, 9).
Anchor-only candidates come from the anchors/ plane.
Generates candidates + statistics only. Never scores, never sorts.
③ BM25F -- rank(), the one scorer both paths call
wtf = Σf wf·tff + anchor·tf_anchor score = Σt idf(t) · wtf·(k1+1) / (wtf + k1·(1 − b + b·wlen/avg_wlen))
idf(t) = ln((n − df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1) wlen = Σf wf·flenf + anchor·alen, derived at query time from committed flen
Weight-then-saturate ONCE -- never per-field BM25 summed. k1 1.2 · b 0.15 · body 1 · heading 3 · title 2 · path 1.5 · ctx 1 · anchor 1 (ON, measured 2026-09-24).
Anchor terms never enter df (idf cannot move for an unrelated doc). A doc matching NONE of the user's own hashes, in body or anchor, is dropped before it is scored.
Document multipliers, ONE Weighting for both paths: [priority] per source entry (longest match wins, unlisted = 1.0) x intent prior 1 + 0.1 when the doc's [doctype]
type matches the question's cue (how do I -> procedure · why -> decision · what is -> reference). Shipped ON, inert until [doctype] declares a type (W-168 step 9).
Sort key (−round(score, 9), superseded, −mtime, −priority, id) -- total and machine-independent. Equal rounded scores are flagged tie. Depth = max(top, 20) when ④ or ⑥ is on.
Top 20, each doc scored by its BEST passage (the refer chunker): score x (1 + w · coverage² · (0.55 + 0.30·min-span + 0.15·bigram adjacency)). Re-orders, never retrieves.
Same uplift, same weight, in answer's rescore. A url: doc keeps its score offline.
A human-pinned doc for this exact question moves to #1 AFTER ranking, inserted if absent, score untouched (0.0 if never scored). Never a score.
⑥ graph compose -- lazy PPR + RRF
Seeds = the lexical top 5, restart mass 1/(rank+1). Lazy PPR over ref edges only: damping 0.85, laziness 0.5, 3 fixed iterations, 1 hop, edge weight = grade,
hub damping 1/(1 + ln(1 + in-degree)) ON here. Tier A: re-order the window by RRF(lexical rank, PPR rank) = Σ 1/(60 + rank). The BM25F score is kept; the row
says boosted and shows its route (#7 -> #2 via graph). Tier B: walked docs (<= 10) holding NONE of the query's hashes -> a labelled related list (<= 5), each with a route.
Tier B is never scored, never in the band. No fresh graph.json = no tier and a stderr note; ask still answers. The pin goes in BEFORE the walk and is never moved by it.
coverage = idf-weighted share of query terms the corpus holds · doc_coverage = the same over the top doc (floor 0.0 = off) · separation = (s1 − s2) / s1 · support = result count
none: nothing scored · partial: a term matches no doc, or cited bytes stale · weak: separation < floor 0.1 · grounded. answerable = band != none; failed names the gate.
weak is a signal, not a refusal (W-214). missing names every absent term -- the field an agent should read first. ask and find fetch nothing, so verified = unverified.
A graph-lifted #1 may LOWER the band, never raise it. Both floors are published in the block. Nothing here can reach a score or an ordering.
Also at query time: -q fuses several questions by RRF (k = 60) and score becomes an RRF score (fused: true). Matched headings (§) are a display-only pick from phrases.
fux lexical = ①-⑤ with mined, intent and graph forced off -- the frozen baseline (SR-CLI d12). find shares Tier A and never computes Tier B. --fast changes speed, never a result.

passage set's own df and n. A

off here, ON inside ask's tier ⑥
exceeding it is reported, never absorbed
title + heading probes in the top 10;
same lenses on fux serve's tabs
NOT IN THE ENGINE -- SO DO NOT LOOK FOR THEM
Deleted: the dense/embedding lane and its score fusion (2026-08-25) · recency, superseded and archived multipliers (W-151, W-152) · RM3 -- failed twice, removed twice (W-224, W-237) ·
the git authority prior -- built at 0.0, measured, lost rank-1 answers at every weight, never released (W-168 step 8; index v6 skipped to v7).
Never built: a cross-encoder reranker (refused on cross-machine determinism, SR-RERANK) · MMR (W-168 step 7, stopped at its gate) · SDM proximity (parked) · a separate exact-identifier
field (families replaced it, SR-IDENTIFIERS) · section records (W-236: SR-SECTIONS proposed, size measured, not built -- the chunker's sections are answer's passages, not index records).
Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/query/, ingest/, derive/, graph/, inspect/, refer/, store/, templates/tune.toml.txt (shipped defaults, L12) and constants.toml (fixed values).
